objective_for_doctor: A 37-year-old F patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: nausea.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve been having nausea and I’ve vomited several times. I also have very severe pain—about 8 out of 10—starting very suddenly (10 out of 10). The pain is in my upper chest and belly/epigastric area, and it radiates to my thoracic spine and my left scapula.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—when did the nausea/vomiting and sudden severe epigastric/upper chest pain start (exact timing), and do you have any shortness of breath, sweating, or feeling faint?  
Doctor: Does the pain worsen with eating or lying down, and have you noticed fever or black/bloody stools?  
Doctor: On a scale of 0–10, how bad is the pain now, and are you pregnant or could you be?

It started very suddenly—about 10 out of 10 pace. I don’t know the exact timing.  

I don’t know about shortness of breath, sweating, or feeling faint.  

I don’t know if it worsens with eating or lying down.  

I don’t know about fever or black/bloody stools.  

The pain is about 8 out of 10 now.  

I don’t know if I’m pregnant or could be.

Doctor: REQUEST TEST: ECG, REQUEST TEST: Troponin, REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP (including AST/ALT, bilirubin), lipase, and pregnancy test (urine/serum hCG).  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Right-upper-quadrant ultrasound and consider CT abdomen/pelvis only if the above don’t explain it—answer me: are you able to take deep breaths without worsening the pain?
I don’t know.

Doctor: I need a quick yes/no: can you take a deep breath without worsening the pain, and do you have any history of gallstones, heavy alcohol use, high triglycerides, or prior ulcers/GERD?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Vitals (BP/HR/RR/O2 sat/T temp) and repeat focused abdominal exam (epigastric/RUQ tenderness, guarding, Murphy sign).  
Doctor: Based on your sudden 10/10-to-8/10 epigastric/upper chest pain radiating to the back/scapula with vomiting, I’m most concerned about pancreatitis or a biliary source—if your ECG/troponin are negative, we’ll prioritize lipase + RUQ ultrasound immediately.
I don’t know.

Doctor: I’m going to treat this as potentially serious—right now, I need you to answer two quick yes/no questions: do you have measured fever (temp ≥38°C) and is the pain mainly in the right upper abdomen rather than the center/epigastrium?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Vitals (BP/HR/RR/O2 sat/T temp), ECG, Troponin, CBC, CMP (AST/ALT, bilirubin), lipase, pregnancy test (urine hCG), and RUQ ultrasound.  
Doctor: While we wait, do you have any pain relief when you sit up and lean forward, or does it stay the same?

Doctor: Right now, do you have any chest tightness/shortness of breath or sweat/clamminess, yes or no?
I don’t know.

I’ve vomited several times.
